clue.text: Old country jazz fan coming to dance

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a hay (or hey) is an old country dance

explanation.surface: A jazz lover takes up folk dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old country' and 'dance' both hint at folk music, but 'Old country' is the definition: the medieval name for China.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the archaic European name for China, a land known since Marco Polo's travels.

clue.text: Thoroughly search most of the valley

indicators.note: most of means the word for valley loses its final letter

parts.note: a combe is a short valley, especially in southern England

explanation.surface: Someone scours nearly all of the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as if drawing a comb through it.

clue.text: Small boy can finally slay the enemy, expending minimal energy

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of slay
expending means the word for the enemy uses up, and so loses, the energy letter

parts.note: time is the enemy, as the saying goes
E, the abbreviation for energy, is a minimal amount of it

explanation.surface: A little lad can finally slay his foe with barely any effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small boy' looks like wordplay; it is the definition, the crippled child in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny Tim is the small, sickly son of Bob Cratchit in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.

clue.text: A dormant drunk in a disorderly state

indicators.note: drunk signals that the letters of a dormant reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sleeping drunk lies in a messy heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without order or plan, haphazardly, describes a disorderly state.

clue.text: Anger in rural establishments — they may kill people

indicators.note: in places the word for anger inside the word for the rural establishments

parts.note: farms are rural establishments
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Rage boils over on country farms, where guns can be lethal.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns and rifles are weapons whose purpose can be deadly, so a descriptive phrase fits them.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about the French and their country — female lacking bigotry

parts.note: into means enthusiastic about
le is French for the

indicators.note: lacking means the country name has the letter for female removed

parts.note: France is the country of the French

explanation.surface: Someone keen on the French and France, but without a woman, shows bigotry.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerance is the refusal to accept other people's views or kinds, which is what bigotry means.

clue.text: Show up with old lover's model

parts.note: an ex is an old lover; the 's means has
to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A former partner's modelling shows someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose someone is to reveal their faults, to show them up in public.

clue.text: Recipe with mayonnaise — very little in that Italian food

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for recipe, from Latin

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for very inside the garlic sauce

parts.note: aioli is a garlic mayonnaise
V is a little of very, its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A recipe using mayonnaise with barely any of it in an Italian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels with a filling, a classic dish from Italy.

clue.text: Fight over one fellow getting stuff for recycling?

indicators.note: over puts the fight on top of the rest, as this is a down entry

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
I is the Roman numeral one
Ron is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out over one man taking things for recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap iron is discarded metal collected to be melted down and reused.

clue.text: Fellow clean, having removed soft muck

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: having removed tells us to take the letter for soft out of the word for clean

parts.note: pure means clean
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A man cleans up, getting rid of soft muck.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure is dung spread on fields, which is muck in the farmyard sense.

clue.text: Break in street with work finished

parts.note: op (opus) is a work, especially of music
over means finished

explanation.surface: Someone pauses in the street once the job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a break in a journey, a short stay before going on.

clue.text: A lone wolf poet's destroyed in a single fierce move

indicators.note: destroyed signals that the letters of a lone wolf poet's are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A solitary poet is ruined in one swift blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from Macbeth, means all at once in one sudden action.

clue.text: Be good enough to satisfy hungry pelican?

definitions.meaning: to be good enough means to meet the requirements
a pelican stores food in its big beak, so feeding it means stuffing that beak

explanation.surface: Something adequate would satisfy a hungry pelican.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be adequate for a purpose; literally a pelican's beak is its bill.

clue.text: What's sweet in big book, lines offering nonsense

indicators.note: in puts the dessert inside the large volume

parts.note: a tome is a big book
a fool is a sweet, a fruit-and-cream pudding
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: A pudding hidden in a big book, with some lines, adds up to nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomfoolery is silly behaviour or foolish talk, a synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Formula for getting fat — I lose it

parts.note: throw is an anagram signal, so throwing the letters A FIT gives fat with I

explanation.surface: A recipe for gaining weight, from someone losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as instructions tells you to shuffle a set of letters into FAT I.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose it is to lose self-control in sudden anger, an idiom for a tantrum.

clue.text: Stand at front of church? Very cold, not dry

indicators.note: not means the letters for dry are left out of the word for very cold

parts.note: bitter means very cold, of weather
TT, teetotal, means dry (not drinking)

explanation.surface: Standing at the church front, someone shivers in the cold without a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A coffin stand is set before the altar at a funeral, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the frame on which a coffin rests, often placed at the front of a church during a funeral.

clue.text: Plant amazing initially, suffering harm when penetrated by insect

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of amazing
when penetrated by puts the insect inside the rearranged letters
suffering signals the letters of harm are distressed into another order

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An amazing plant suffers harm when an insect bores into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a verb (to bury or place), but here it is the noun, a type of flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranth is a genus of flowering plants, some grown as grain or with showy red flowers.

clue.text: What's in title of poem by Coleridge or Frost

definitions.text: What's in title of poem by Coleridge
definitions.meaning: Coleridge wrote The ... of the Ancient Mariner
frost here is the ice crystals on grass, not the poet Robert Frost

explanation.surface: A question about a word in poem titles by Coleridge or Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the American poet beside Coleridge; it is the second definition, hoar frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is an old spelling of rhyme used in Coleridge's title, and also a white coating of frozen droplets.

clue.text: For example, a space to the north where a boat may berth

indicators.note: to the north means read upwards, backwards in a down entry

parts.note: e.g. means for example
room is space

explanation.surface: A northern berth gives space for a boat, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' reverses EGAROOM, as the entry runs down.
explanation.definitionFit: A moorage is a place where a vessel can be tied up and kept.

clue.text: Mum entertained by Jagger et al performing — one getting into rock?

indicators.note: entertained by puts the word for mum inside the band name

parts.note: Mick Jagger and his bandmates are the (Rolling) Stones
ma is mum
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: Mick Jagger's band plays to their mother, rock stars indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests rock music after Jagger; it means stone, which a mason cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason works stone, cutting into rock to shape it, punning on the music genre.

clue.text: Be covered in fleece as female animal

indicators.note: covered in places be inside the word for clip a fleece

parts.note: to shear is to fleece, clip the wool off

explanation.surface: An animal wrapped in wool turns out to be female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a noun for wool but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-bear is a bear of the female sex, a sow.

clue.text: England's all-rounder gets all fired up

definitions.meaning: England's cricket all-rounder, batting and bowling
to fire up is to feed a fire, as a stoker does

explanation.surface: England's star cricketer becomes passionately excited.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-rounder in cricket is a player who both bats and bowls well.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Stokes is the England cricketer, and stokes means feeds a fire to make it fiercer.

clue.text: Fruit ruined by terrible shower

indicators.note: ruined by tells us the letters of terrible shower are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A crop of fruit is spoilt by a terrible downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Whortleberries are bilberries, small dark berries growing on heathland shrubs.

clue.text: Flatter shade of brown

definitions.meaning: to flatter here is the verb, to curry favour servilely
a light yellowish-brown colour, like a young deer

explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to flatter slavishly, and fawn is a pale brown colour named after the young deer.

clue.text: Tale-teller is candid, love being rejected

parts.note: frank means candid

indicators.note: being rejected means the word for love is turned back to front

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, nil

explanation.surface: A storyteller is honest, though love is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Franklin, a landowner, tells one of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Franklin is one of the pilgrims in The Canterbury Tales who tells a story on the way.

clue.text: A new hair product possibly needed by a lady

parts.note: gel is one example of a hair product

explanation.surface: A lady might need a new styling product for her hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's given name, so it stands for an unnamed lady.

clue.text: Part of Greece has style that's unusual

indicators.note: that's unusual says the letters of has style are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A region of Greece has an unusual style.
explanation.definitionFit: Thessaly is a region of central Greece, a broad plain home to Mount Olympus's foothills.

clue.text: Batty woman returning to quiet plain in Israel

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: returning means the woman's name is read backwards

parts.note: Nora Batty is a character in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine

explanation.surface: A crazy woman goes back to the quiet plains of Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' looks like 'mad'; it is a surname, from Nora Batty of the long-running British TV comedy Last of the Summer Wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sharon plain is a coastal lowland in Israel, between Haifa and Tel Aviv.
